memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine review of vitamin D deficiency, IBS and GERD.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports mild epigastric discomfort after meals, occasional bloating and constipation. No alarm symptoms.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/86 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 1.55 m, BMI 28.3 (obese). Abdomen soft, non‑tender, no organomegaly.
IMPRESSION: 1) Vitamin D deficiency – level unknown pending labs. 2) Irritable bowel syndrome, stable. 3) Gastro‑oesophageal reflux, controlled on current pantoprazole.
ARRANGEMENTS: Advise weight reduction through balanced diet and daily 30‑min walk. Start cholecalciferol 60 000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks then 1000 IU daily. Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS for IBS. Continue pantoprazole 40 mg OD before breakfast, domperidone 10 mg BD before meals, antacid gel SOS. Order fasting lipid profile, fasting blood sugar, serum 25‑OH‑vit D, calcium, phosphate, CBC, stool routine, tTG‑IgA. Return if: new dysphagia, unintentional weight loss, vomiting, fever >39 °C, or blood in stools.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been taking the vitamin D granules as prescribed. My bloating has improved a bit but I still get heartburn after spicy food. Should I continue the antacid gel?

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: follow‑up on vitamin D replacement and symptom review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She says bloating is less frequent, heartburn occurs twice a week after meals, no constipation.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/84, weight 66.5 kg, BMI 27.7 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no tenderness.
IMPRESSION: Vitamin D deficiency improving but still low. IBS symptoms mild. GERD controlled with occasional antacid use.
ARRANGEMENTS: Encourage continued weight loss; aim for <65 kg. Increase cholecalciferol to 2000 IU OD after completing loading course. Continue mebeverine BD, ispaghula husk OD, loperamide SOS. Continue pantoprazole OD, domperidone BD, antacid gel SOS. Repeat vitamin D level in 6 weeks. Return if: worsening heartburn, dysphagia, vomiting, fever >39 °C, or rectal bleeding.

memories.text: Upper GI endoscopy: mucosa shows mild erythema in antrum, no ulceration. Biopsy negative for H. pylori and malignancy.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Refer to Dr. S. Rao, Gastroenterology, for evaluation of persistent GERD symptoms despite PPI therapy.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Specialist notes: mild gastritis, no Barrett’s epithelium. Recommend continue pantoprazole 40 mg OD, lifestyle modification, and repeat endoscopy in 1 year if symptoms persist.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine check‑up, review of gastro‑intestinal symptoms and vitamin D status.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports occasional heartburn after heavy meals, no bloating, bowel movements regular.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/88, weight 65.8 kg, BMI 27.3 (overweight). Abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: Vitamin D now sufficient. IBS asymptomatic. GERD controlled on pantoprazole.
ARRANGEMENTS: Maintain weight <65 kg with diet and walks. Continue cholecalciferol 2000 IU OD. Continue mebeverine BD only if symptoms recur; otherwise stop. Continue ispaghula husk OD, loperamide SOS. Pantoprazole OD, domperidone BD, antacid gel SOS. Order fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar (annual). Return if: new dysphagia, unintentional weight loss, vomiting, fever >39 °C, or melena.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: 6‑month review of vitamin D, IBS and GERD.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She feels well, no heartburn, no bloating, regular bowel motions.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82, weight 64.9 kg, BMI 27.0 (overweight). Abdomen soft, non‑tender.
IMPRESSION: Vitamin D adequate. IBS in remission. GERD well controlled.
ARRANGEMENTS: Advise maintain weight <64 kg via Mediterranean‑style diet and 30‑min brisk walk 5 days/week. Reduce cholecalciferol to maintenance 1000 IU OD. Stop mebeverine (symptom‑free). Continue ispaghula husk OD, loperamide SOS. Continue pantoprazole OD, domperidone BD, antacid gel SOS. Influenza vaccine offered; patient declined (egg allergy). Return if: dysphagia, odynophagia, vomiting, fever >39 °C, or rectal bleeding.
